op_constraints: op-subset (ops_supported.json): FFT stages cannot slice/index-register values; partner/group values are fetched via address-computed GM loads inside one kernel (in-kernel scratch ping-pong). Constraints: supported = load/store(addr-arithmetic gather), where(same shape), //, %, cos/sin, full sum; unsupported = slice, reg/scalar index, trans, sum(axis), join/split/cat, chained None, python math in jit; reshape passes the frontend but crashes the XPU lowering (GlobalEncodingAttr UNREACHABLE) -> no kernel here uses reshape.  NOTE (stale-read bug): the GM ping-pong pattern is unreliable: store->permuted-load from the same buffer returns stale values at grid>1 (this WP) and — per WP3's size sweep — also at grid=1 for n=32/64; see wp2_concurrency.json and wp3_blockmax.json.  The scalar codegen kernel sidesteps the whole op-subset: unrolling happens in python, the jit body is pure scalar load/compute/store.

cases.ownership: grid=1 program owns the whole packet: input load, all log2(N) DIT stages, output store; registers v_re/v_im are the packet-private live set
cases.local_live_data_range: register v (2x16B fp32 SoA) across 3 stages; GM scratch ping-pong S0/S1 (2x2x16B)
required_global_boundaries: scratch S0/S1 (per-stage partner load + stage store)
cases.synchronization_scope: single program; in-program program-order RAW only; no barrier, no cross-program sync (grid=1)

expected_gm_bytes.formula: 4*N*4 (stage0 v+b loads) + (L-1)*2*N*4 (partner loads) + (L-1)*2*N*4 (scratch stores) + 2*N*4 (final stores), L=log2(N)
